maplibre_worker_bug.real_browser_verification: PASSED -- the project owner independently opened http://localhost:3002/fifteen-minute in their own real desktop browser after the fix and confirmed the map renders correctly. This is NOT listed as a remaining product limitation.
maplibre_worker_bug.root_cause: MapLibre GL JS 6.x loads a separate worker script (maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, plus its own dependency maplibre-gl-shared.mjs) via a runtime-computed import.meta.url-relative path. Next.js's webpack build could not statically detect this pattern (MapLibre wraps the URL computation in a helper function), so the worker file was never emitted into the build output. The resulting Worker was constructed against a URL serving nothing -- silently, with no thrown error -- so every tile-load request was dispatched and never answered.
maplibre_worker_bug.fix: Copied both required files into public/ and called MapLibre's own documented setWorkerUrl() API in components/MapView.tsx before constructing any Map. Automated via a new `npm run sync-maplibre-worker` script wired into `postinstall`, so this survives a fresh install or a future maplibre-gl version bump.

Production build succeeds, production server runs, all routes work, optimized data joins correctly (12/12 integrity checks), navigation is stable through a full client-side stress test with the map rendering, the security audit is clean (0 vulnerabilities, reconfirmed after a clean install), and responsive layout passes at all 3 required viewports with the map visible.
